# PRD

## Title
MS MARCO Passage Search App

## Summary
Build a local search application with a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The app will search over the MS MARCO passage corpus and show randomly selected sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev query set so users can try realistic searches immediately.

## Problem
We need a simple end-to-end application for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval through Anserini. Today, retrieval is available through backend tools, but there is no lightweight web app that lets users search the corpus and test example queries easily.

## Goals
- Search the MS MARCO passage corpus through the Anserini REST API server.
- Provide a Next.js frontend for entering queries and viewing ranked results.
- Show random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries on each page load.
- Make the app easy to run locally for development and demos.

## Non-Goals
- Training or fine-tuning models
- Building a custom search backend
- Authentication or user accounts
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Multi-corpus support

## Users
- Developers and researchers exploring retrieval behavior
- Demo users who want to try realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running the frontend and backend

## Core Requirements
- Use the repo-local Anserini skills as the source of truth: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.
- Start by installing the Anserini fatjar via `install-anserini-fatjar` and confirm that it has been correctly installed.
- Use the Anserini REST API server as the backend. Do not guess the routes or the shape of the responses; read the relevant repo-local Anserini skill docs first, especially `anserini-cli` for REST examples.
- Search over the MS MARCO passage corpus.
- Build the frontend in Next.js.
- Show several randomly selected sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev set.
- Let users click a sample query to run it.
- Display ranked search results.
- Handle empty queries, no-results states, and backend errors clearly.
- Use backend port `8080` and frontend port `3000` by default. Make both ports configurable through environment variables, but do not stop to ask the user for port choices.

## UX
On page load, the user sees a search input and a set of sample queries. The user can type a query or click a sample query. The app sends the query to the Anserini backend and displays ranked passage results.

## Success Criteria
- Users can submit queries and receive ranked MS MARCO passage results.
- Sample queries are visible and usable on load.
- The app works end-to-end in a local environment with clear frontend/backend configuration.

Build a local search application with a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The app will search over the MS MARCO passage corpus and show randomly selected sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev query set so users can try realistic searches immediately.

## Problem
We need a simple end-to-end application for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval through Anserini. Today, retrieval is available through backend tools, but there is no lightweight web app that lets users search the corpus and test example queries easily.

## Goals
- Search the MS MARCO passage corpus through the Anserini REST API server.
- Provide a Next.js frontend for entering queries and viewing ranked results.
- Show random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries on each page load.
- Make the app easy to run locally for development and demos.

## Non-Goals
- Training or fine-tuning models
- Building a custom search backend
- Authentication or user accounts
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Multi-corpus support

## Users
- Developers and researchers exploring retrieval behavior
- Demo users who want to try realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running the frontend and backend

## Core Requirements
- Use the repo-local Anserini skills as the source of truth: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.
- Start by installing the Anserini fatjar via `install-anserini-fatjar` and confirm that it has been correctly installed.
- Use the Anserini REST API server as the backend. Do not guess the routes or the shape of the responses; read the relevant repo-local Anserini skill docs first, especially `anserini-cli` for REST examples.
- Search over the MS MARCO passage corpus.
- Build the frontend in Next.js.
- Show several randomly selected sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev set.
- Let users click a sample query to run it.
- Display ranked search results.
- Handle empty queries, no-results states, and backend errors clearly.
- Use backend port `8080` and frontend port `3000` by default. Make both ports configurable through environment variables, but do not stop to ask the user for port choices.

## UX
On page load, the user sees a search input and a set of sample queries. The user can type a query or click a sample query. The app sends the query to the Anserini backend and displays ranked passage results.

## Success Criteria
- Users can submit queries and receive ranked MS MARCO passage results.
- Sample queries are visible and usable on load.
- The app works end-to-end in a local environment with clear frontend/backend configuration.

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.

# PRD

## Title

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display

# PRD

## Title

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample

# PRD

## Title

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MAR

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Problem

- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure

Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corp

# PRD

The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Non-Goals

- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

-

- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining

# PRD

## Title

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo

- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying

# PRD

## Summary

The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements

# PRD

## Title

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem

- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative:

- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anser

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fat

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`,

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anser

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. - Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.

- Authentication or user account functionality

- Support for multiple corpora

- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli

Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. - Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anser

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-re

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.
- First

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.
- First install the Anser

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.
- First install the Anserini fat

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.
- First install the Anserini fatjar using `install-anser

# PRD

## Title

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.
- First install the Anserini fatjar using `install-anserini-fat

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

- First install the Anserini fatjar using `install-anserini-fatjar`, then verify

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.
- First install the Anserini fatjar using `install-anserini-fatjar`, then verify that the installation succeeded

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.
- First install the Anserini fatjar using `install-anserini-fatjar`, then verify that the installation succeeded.

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.
- First install the Anserini fatjar using `install-anserini-fatjar`, then verify that the installation succeeded.
- Use the Anserini

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.
- First install the Anserini fatjar using `install-anserini-fatjar`, then verify that the installation succeeded.
- Use the Anserini REST API

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.
- First install the Anserini fatjar using `install-anserini-fatjar`, then verify that the installation succeeded.
- Use the Anserini REST API server for the backend

Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.

- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals

- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

# PRD

## Title

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.
- First install the Anserini fatjar using `install-anserini-fatjar`, then verify that the installation succeeded.
- Use the Anserini REST API server for the backend. Do not infer

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.
- First install the Anserini fatjar using `install-anserini-fatjar`, then verify that the installation succeeded.
- Use the Anserini REST API server for the backend. Do not infer API routes

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.
- First install the Anserini fatjar using `install-anserini-fatjar`, then verify that the installation succeeded.
- Use the Anserini REST API server for the backend. Do not infer API routes or response

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.
- First install the Anserini fatjar using `install-anserini-fatjar`, then verify that the installation succeeded.
- Use the Anserini REST API server for the backend. Do not infer API routes or response formats;

# PRD

## Title

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem

- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

- First install the Anserini fatjar using `install-anserini-fatjar`, then verify that the installation succeeded.

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.
- First install the Anserini fatjar using `install-anserini-fatjar`, then verify that the installation succeeded.
- Use the Anserini REST API server for the backend. Do not infer API routes or response formats; first read the relevant repo-local

# PRD

## Title
Local MS MARCO Passage Search Application

## Summary
Create a locally runnable search app consisting of a Next.js frontend and an Anserini REST API backend. The application must retrieve over the MS MARCO passage corpus and present randomly chosen example queries from the MS MARCO passage development query set so users can immediately try realistic searches.

## Problem
An end-to-end, lightweight web interface is needed for exploring MS MARCO passage retrieval with Anserini. Although retrieval functionality exists through backend tooling, there is not currently a simple local web app for searching the corpus and experimenting with example queries.

## Goals
- Query the MS MARCO passage corpus using the Anserini REST API server.
- Implement a Next.js frontend where users can enter queries and inspect ranked results.
- Display random sample queries from the MS MARCO passage dev queries whenever the page loads.
- Keep local development and demo setup straightforward.

## Non-Goals
- Model training or fine-tuning
- Implementing a custom search backend
- Authentication or user account functionality
- Production deployment infrastructure
- Support for multiple corpora

## Users
- Developers and researchers examining retrieval behavior
- Demo users interested in trying realistic benchmark queries
- Local operators running both the frontend and backend services

## Core Requirements
- Treat the repo-local Anserini skills as authoritative: `install-anserini-fatjar`, `anserini-cli`, and `anserini-reproduction`.
- First install the Anserini fatjar using `install-anserini-fatjar`, then verify that the installation succeeded.
- Use the Anserini REST API server for the backend. Do not infer API routes or response formats; first read the relevant repo-local Anser
